q-68609.name: Question 1
q-68609.worked_solution:
To raise the product of two numbers to the power of $4$, we can raise each number to the power of $4,$ and then multiply:

$$
(4\times 2)^{4}={4}^{4}\times {2}^{4}
$$

q-100648.name: Question 2
q-100648.worked_solution:
To raise the product of two numbers to the power of $3$, we can raise each number to the power of $3,$ and then multiply:

$$
(4\times 19)^{3}=({4}^{3})\times ({19}^{3})={4}^{3}\times {19}^{3}
$$

Now, using, ${4}^{3}=64,$ we can simplify:

$$
{4}^{3}\times {19}^{3}=64\times {19}^{3}
$$

q-68613.name: Question 4
q-68613.worked_solution:
To raise the product of two numbers to the power of $8$, we can raise each number to the power of $8,$ and then multiply:

$$

q-68445.name: Question 6
q-68445.worked_solution:
Notice that $-2=(-1)\times 2.$

To raise the product of two numbers to the power of $7$, we can raise each number to the power of $7,$ and then multiply:

$$
(-2)^{7}={((-1)\times 2)}^{7}=(-1)^{7}\times {2}^{7}
$$

Since $-1$ raised to an odd power is $-1,$ we get

$$
(-1)^{7}\times {2}^{7}=(-1)\times {2}^{7}=-{2}^{7}.
$$
